findings.title: Clothesline hazard unfixed: boom/line 0.80–1.0 m above the snow 1–2 m behind the rider in every run
findings.detail: Own recompute (FILM, riding): 1 m behind the pivot min 0.82 m (p10 of case minima 0.852), 2 m behind min 0.799 m. Developer's own ≥2.0 m gate fails in 39/39 runs; developer states no body exit can fix it in carving. Bystander line force 4.5 N (crossing pole), boom impact 1.7 N·s ≈34 N at shoulder height. Kills piste use without written resort permission; this is an envelope limit (empty/low-traffic slopes), not a metric pass.

findings.title: avail pass depends on tolerating a permanent boom artefact (<3 % of subject height) and is knife-edge
findings.detail: The boom is correctly counted in A.art, but it is over the rider in 100 % of filming frames (≈4.5 px wide end-on stub, art p50 0.6–1.1 %). criteria.js says no ≥1 px artefact over the subject → strict avail 0 %. With the 3 % tolerance (also used in round 2) avail 81.5 % reproduces exactly, margin 1.5 pp: hc 0.5 → 80.0 %, mass +15 % → 79.4 %, reefed-glide 70 % → 79.6 %, L/D 0.6 → 73.0 %, all-adverse 63.5 %. Tailwind ≥6 m/s bins 39–80 %.

findings.title: Active boom gimbal is undersized vs its own simulated demand
findings.detail: Boom 60 g over 1.2 m: static gravity torque ≈0.353 N·m horizontal, p99 dynamic torque 0.121–0.965 N·m (pointing τ 20 ms), plus a ≈90 g KCU seated on the tip during each 2.8 s stow (≈1 N·m). Budget: 2 × 40 g brushless gimbal motors, 1.5 W, kill test written at 0.13 N·m. Gimbal motors of that class deliver ≈0.05–0.15 N·m; a geared actuator adds mass/volume/power. The active boom is load-bearing: passive boom ablation → avail 42.9 %.
findings.evidence: audit3/kite2/out_recheck_all.json agg.boom; sim/js/concepts/kite2/model.js PDEF (boomMass, tauBoomAct, pGimbal); dev results sensitivity passive_boom

findings.title: Heave-compensating winch is idealised: perfect zero-lag feed-forward, no motor speed/voltage limit
findings.detail: nuHC = exact exit velocity along the line (no sensor lag/noise) added after the slew limiter; reel-in under load reaches 6.341–7.98 m/s at 8–16 N, motoring peaks 93–166 W, line acceleration up to 172.112 m/s². With the model's own Kt 0.012 N·m/A, 6:1, 12 mm drum this needs ≈40–50 V back-EMF (max line speed 1.85 m/s at 11.1 V); power and I²R loss are therefore computed for an impossible operating point. A drone-class motor with lower gearing could plausibly do it (not a kill), but the 70 g winch budget and the endurance figure are unverified. Sensitivity: hc 0.5 → avail 80.04 % (pass by 0.04 pp), KE 13.1 J; hc 0 → 79.7 % FAIL (dev ablation). No parameter caps total line speed, so a true speed-limit test needs a model change.

findings.title: headClear margin is 10 cm and excludes the worn boom (0.42 m from the helmet centre)
findings.detail: Own geometry reproduces 1.105 m (crossL cases, line just beyond the boom tip). Declared exclusion windows 2.76–2.82 s (≤3 s, compliant); inside them the seated KCU is 0.563 m from the helmet centre. Boom segment 0.423 m, tip 0.661 m from the helmet centre whenever extended — not 'airborne' under criteria.js, but an actuated rigid tube near the head in a fall/collision. Fault case (winch failure at a stop) 0.815 m (dev).

findings.title: Wind gates honest; in-flight control and tip-pitot check use noise-free local true wind
findings.detail: Launch, park, stop and retrieve-planning gates read windEstimate() (fullrun.js) — compliant. The launch confirmation (tip pitot, model.js ~L516) and the in-flight wind-window controller (eaW from true local wind, 40 ms filter) are noise-free sensor idealisations, not oracle case-mean wind. Setup is simulated (arm tap 2 s constant only); ops from the event log.

findings.title: Polar sensitivities disclosed honestly; avail fails at the documented-low end
findings.detail: Default L/D lowered to 0.75 (MC-1-1C) and reefed retention 0.5 (no data). KE, force and headClear no longer depend on them (verified by dev sensitivities, KE 12.9–13.0 J). avail: L/D 0.6 → 73.0 %, retention 0.7-loss → 79.6 %, mass +15 % → 79.4 %, combined 63.5 % — the concept passes only at nominal assumptions.

safetyRegulatory: Written resort permission is a hard gate: line/boom 0.8–1.0 m above the snow behind the rider (A3-K2-01).
Rigid actuated boom 0.42 m from the helmet centre and at shoulder height for crossing skiers (≈34 N, 1.7 N·s).
KE 12.9 J governed (≤14.9 J line) only while the soft clutch works; fault cases separate.
Kite ≤14 m line: outside drone rules in most jurisdictions but subject to kite/tethered-object rules near lifts.
credibleEnvelope: Simulation-credible only on empty/low-traffic pistes with written permission, rider 7–16 m/s, head/cross/calm wind 0–9 m/s (tailwind ≥6 m/s → 39–80 %), and only if: canopy L/D ≥≈0.7 with ≥50 % reefed-glide retention, a boom gimbal that holds ≤0.5° pointing under ≈0.4–1 N·m, a heave-comp winch with ≤30 ms lag at 6–8 m/s, a 45° trumpet dock, and a custom 60° 4K optic — and if a permanent few-pixel boom stub over the rider is accepted as footage.
verdict: Reproduces exactly (39/39) and passes all 13 judged metrics as modelled with the developer-tolerant artefact rule (avail 81.5 %, jitter p90 1.66, setup 4.7 s, ops 1, F 28.1 N, KE 12.9 J, headClear 1.105 m, endurance 56.9 min). Safety metrics are now robust; footage availability is knife-edge (≤1.5 pp margin, fails at L/D 0.6, mass +15 %, or a strict ≥1 px artefact rule) and rests on two idealised actuators (zero-lag heave winch beyond its own motor model; a gimbal driving a 1.2 m boom with motors too small for its simulated torque). The clothesline hazard is unfixed by design. Verdict: conditional pass as a research concept; not a usable product until tow/bench tests settle polar, gimbal, winch and dock.
